summary:
Medora is an AI-powered astronaut health monitoring and prediction system that we developed to go beyond current health monitoring systems used in space missions. While existing systems mainly measure astronauts' current health conditions, we took a step further by using AI and Machine Learning to predict their future health conditions.

We process real-time health measurements collected during space missions through five specialized ML models trained with NASA datasets. These models predict future health conditions of five major organs: the brain, heart, lungs, kidneys, and bones.

We also developed an AI Agent that analyzes predictions from all five models together. It also uses historical astronaut health reports from previous NASA missions through a RAG system to provide deeper analysis beyond individual ML predictions.

A main highlight of Medora is its interactive 3D human anatomy environment with voice-based interaction, allowing astronauts to explore organs and understand their health conditions. The system also includes a health analysis dashboard with interactive graphs showing real-time measurements, future predictions, and historical data from similar missions.

Overall, Medora combines Machine Learning, AI Agents, historical mission data, and interactive 3D visualization to provide better prediction and understanding of astronaut health during space missions.
details:
MEDORA AI – Predictive Astronaut Health Intelligence

About Our Project

Astronauts face many health challenges during space missions. Living in microgravity, exposure to space radiation, stress, and spending long periods away from Earth can affect different parts of their bodies. Although astronauts already use medical devices to monitor their health, we wanted to take this idea one step further.

Our project, Medora AI, is an intelligent astronaut health monitoring and prediction platform that aims to predict future health risks instead of only showing current health measurements.

Our main idea is simple. What if astronauts could not only see their current health condition but also understand what might happen to their health in the next few hours or days?

That is what we are trying to achieve with Medora AI.

How Our System Works

Medora is designed to collect real-time health measurements from astronauts, including heart rate, oxygen saturation, breathing rate, body temperature, and other available health information.

These measurements are passed through a feature engineering pipeline, where the data is cleaned, organized, and prepared for machine learning predictions.

After that, the processed information is sent to five machine learning models that focus on five main body systems:

  • Heart: Predicts changes in heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen related measurements, and possible cardiovascular risks.
  • Brain: Focuses on cognitive health, including attention, memory, response time, and stress-related changes.
  • Lungs: Predicts changes in breathing patterns, oxygen saturation, and possible respiratory risks.
  • Kidneys: Focuses on fluid balance, urine output, and possible kidney-related health risks.
  • Bones: Predicts longer-term changes in bone health and possible musculoskeletal risks.

Each model is designed to predict health changes over a relevant time period. This allows our system to consider both short-term and longer-term risks.

For developing our prediction models, we use NASA datasets and improve them to match the input parameters required by our system. We clean, process, and apply feature engineering to the datasets to extract the important health measurements needed for our five ML models. This helps us prepare suitable training data to predict future health conditions and identify possible risks for astronauts.

AI Agent for Health Analysis

Another important part of Medora is our AI agent.

Once the five ML models generate their predictions, the results are passed to our AI agent for deeper analysis.

The agent analyzes predictions from different body systems together, identifies possible connections, and provides detailed insights into future health risks and their potential effects on astronauts.

We developed the agent using LangGraph, LangChain, RAG, tool calling, Qdrant, and a large language model to combine ML predictions with relevant medical knowledge.

The AI agent goes beyond basic predictions of ML mo by providing deeper health analysis, explaining possible risks, and suggesting areas that may need further attention.

Interactive 3D Anatomy and Voice Recognition

Most creative feature of Medora is our interactive 3D human anatomy environment

We also developed a voice recognition system that allows astronauts to control the 3D model using simple voice commands.

This makes Medora more convenient for astronauts, especially during space missions when they may be busy with other tasks or have difficulty using traditional controls. Instead of manually navigating through different pages, astronauts can use their voice to quickly access the health information they need.

By combining 3D anatomy with voice recognition, Medora provides a simpler, more interactive, and hands-free way for astronauts to understand their health and future risks.

Predictive Health Analysis Dashboard

Medora also includes an analysis dashboard that brings together three important types of information.

The first is the health data collected during the mission.

The second is the future health predictions generated by our machine learning models.

The third is historical health information that can be used to compare similar conditions and identify patterns.

By combining these, the dashboard aims to show how an astronaut's health is changing, what future trends the models predict, and whether there are signs of possible health risks.

This is important because astronauts and medical teams need to understand not only individual measurements but also how those measurements change over time.

Technologies We Used

We used several technologies to develop different parts of Medora AI.

For our frontend, we use Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Three.js, React Three Fiber, and Drei to build the user interface and interactive 3D anatomy environment.

For our backend, we use Spring Boot 4, PostgreSQL, and Flyway to manage application services, data storage, and database migrations.

For the prediction models, we use Python, XGBoost, CatBoost, scikit-learn, pandas, NumPy, and other machine learning libraries. We also use FastAPI to connect prediction services with the rest of our system.

For the AI agent, our technology stack includes LangChain, LangGraph, Qdrant, FastEmbed, embedding models, and LLM integration.

Our project also uses Microsoft Azure and Neon for deployment and database hosting components.

What Makes Our Project Creative?

The main creativity of Medora is not just using AI or building another health monitoring system.

Our idea is to connect five health prediction models, an AI agent, interactive 3D anatomy, voice recognition, and a predictive analysis dashboard into one platform.

Many monitoring systems focus on showing measurements. Medora aims to help users understand how those measurements may change in the future and what those changes could mean.

We also wanted to make complicated health information easier to understand. That is why we introduced interactive anatomy, voice commands, and AI-generated explanations rather than depending only on traditional medical graphs.

Another important part of our approach is analyzing multiple body systems together. Health conditions can be connected, so our AI agent is designed to look at predictions across different systems instead of treating every prediction separately.

Our Vision

With Medora AI, we want to move from simply monitoring astronauts' health to understanding how their health could change in the future.

Our vision is to help astronauts stay one step ahead of possible health risks, making future space exploration safer and more informed.
